pr.title: Add field uninstall: the installer's uninstall target removes what the installer made (install.md §3.5)
pr.head: ef4ef2e63f74e5a00c04da7e93e61aa227b5fac2

summary: Field installs in one of two ways. A release install is what curl -fsSL https://field.one/install.sh | bash makes: the installer, install.sh, downloads a release's source into a directory of its own under ~/.local/share/field, builds it there, and puts a two-line script, the shim, at ~/.local/bin/field to run it. A checkout install is a clone that pnpm's global field links to. Before this change, removing a release install meant an rm -rf from the docs, and removing a checkout install meant knowing to run pnpm remove -g field.

This change adds an uninstall target to install.sh, and a field uninstall command that runs it the way field upgrade runs the installer. In a release install, the target removes only what the installer can show it made, by the same tests the installer already uses to prune old versions, and it keeps everything else with a kept row. In a checkout install, it removes pnpm's link only when that link points at this checkout, and it never deletes the checkout.

The review left two findings open, both on install.sh. The row about model weights names only the Hugging Face cache, but the ACE-Step worker keeps its ~10 GB in ~/.field/models/acestep. The uninstall also deletes a Field shim that runs a different data directory, which orphans that install while it reports uninstalled.

Left for later: field.one/uninstall.sh, a static file in okamnesiac/audiofield that runs this target. It can deploy only after a release carries the target, because 0.3.0's installer rejects uninstall.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Data directory (DATA_DIR): where release installs live. It is FIELD_DATA_DIR when set, otherwise $XDG_DATA_HOME/field or ~/.local/share/field.
  • Bin directory (BIN_DIR): where the shim goes. It is FIELD_BIN_DIR, then what release.conf recorded, then ~/.local/bin.
  • Version: a directory named X.Y.Z holding one built release. The installer counts it as its own only when it is a real directory, not a symlink, whose install.sh carries SHIM_MARKER, the comment line every shim starts with.
  • Download: .download-X.Y.Z, the staging directory a release unpacks in, counted only when it holds unpacked/.
  • current: the symlink naming the version the shim runs.
  • release.conf: the repository, ref, and bin directory the install follows.
  • Fetch cache: cache/fetchcontent, JUCE's download, which every version's daemon build shares.
  • prune: the installer step that removes old versions after an upgrade, using the same two tests.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• Both full reviews of ef4ef2e request changes. Two P2 finding threads remain open: the shim for another data directory is deleted, and ACE-Step weights are misreported.
  • The gpt-6 review passes pnpm typecheck, project check, and bash -n install.sh. It independently reproduces the shim deletion with a temporary bin directory and confirms that the other installation survives without its launcher.
  • The install plan stays in-progress. Its earlier question about the installer domain remains open; this change introduces no new question.

groups.title: The installer's uninstall target
groups.kicker: install.sh learns to remove what it installed, and nothing else
intro: install.sh already had five targets: all, cli, audiod, workers, and status. It runs each one in one of two modes. When the script sits in a git work tree beside src/cli.ts, it is a checkout installer. Otherwise, piped from curl or downloaded by field upgrade, it is a release installer. This group adds uninstall to both modes.

In release mode, uninstall_release has to work in a data directory that may hold other things, because FIELD_DATA_DIR can point anywhere. So it removes a directory only when the installer can show it made it. A version is a real X.Y.Z directory whose install.sh carries SHIM_MARKER. A download is .download-X.Y.Z with unpacked/ inside. Both tests are the ones prune uses after an upgrade. The shim goes first, so field never runs a version that is half removed. The target then removes current, release.conf, and JUCE's download, and removes the data directory only if it is empty.
In checkout mode, uninstall_checkout runs pnpm remove -g field only when pnpm's global field links this checkout, and it always leaves the checkout itself.

files.note: Adds uninstall_release, uninstall_checkout, and huggingface_cache, wires uninstall into both modes and the usage line, and changes the header to lead with field.one.

checks.text: This is the "nothing installed" test. It also passes when the bin directory holds a Field shim and the data directory holds no version, which is the case the flag at line 956 is about.

Open finding: the shim is removed whenever it carries SHIM_MARKER, without checking that it runs this data directory's current. Install with FIELD_DATA_DIR=/custom/field, then run the curl uninstall without it, and the target deletes the shim and prints uninstalled, while every version in /custom/field stays. The shim was the only record of where that install lives. The fix is to remove the shim only when it runs $DATA_DIR/current/dist/cli.js, and otherwise keep it with a row naming its data directory.
The removal loop calls the existing ownership tests before deleting version or download directories. The focused installer tests exercise foreign files and directories that must survive.

Nothing stops or names a running field-audiod before its version goes. An idle daemon exits by itself after 300 seconds. A playing one never goes idle, so it keeps running from the deleted binary, and no field is left to stop it. The review lists this as a suggestion.

release.conf and the fetch cache go with no ownership test. docs/install.md already tells you to give FIELD_DATA_DIR a directory of Field's own, because the installer writes current, release.conf, and cache/ there.

Open finding: this row names only the Hugging Face cache, but field-aced downloads its ~10 GB of ACE-Step weights into ~/.field/models/acestep. models_root in python/aced/src/field_aced/adapter.py picks that directory, and the files never enter the Hugging Face cache. A user who follows the row clears the wrong directory. The fix is to also name $FIELD_ACE_MODELS, or ~/.field/models when it is unset, and to correct the comment, the docs, and plan §3.5.
The checkout uninstall calls pnpm remove -g field only when the resolved global link matches this checkout. The focused tests cover both its own link and another checkout’s link.

groups.title: field uninstall, the command
groups.kicker: A doorway to the installer's target, found the way field upgrade finds it
intro: field upgrade already runs the right installer for the install it runs from. A checkout runs its own install.sh. A release install downloads the newest installer for the repository and ref in release.conf into a temporary directory, and tells it where the data directory is with FIELD_DATA_DIR. With FIELD_OFFLINE set, a release install runs the installed version's own copy instead.
uninstall() refuses on Windows with a message naming pnpm remove -g field, then calls upgrade('uninstall'), so the command shares all of that. Its exit status is the installer's.

files.note: Adds uninstall(): a Windows refusal, then upgrade('uninstall', deps).

checks.text: The earlier review exercised uninstall through a release shim both offline and with an installer downloaded through a local file URL. This command delegates to the same installer path that upgrade already uses.
Errors raised inside upgrade() still say cannot upgrade: … when you ran field uninstall, such as a failed download. The review lists this as a suggestion.

files.note: Registers field uninstall and sets process.exitCode to what the installer returned.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The real installer under bash against stand-ins, and the command's handoff
intro: src/install.test.ts runs the real install.sh with bash, against a temporary HOME and a PATH that holds only stand-ins for pnpm, cmake, curl, and the field CLI, plus links to ordinary tools. Nothing installed on the machine can answer in their place. This change adds rmdir to those tools, a remove -g branch to the pnpm stand-in, and an install.sh uninstall block of eight cases.
src/commands/upgrade.test.ts checks that field uninstall hands a stand-in installer the uninstall target and returns its exit status, and that it refuses on Windows.

checks.text: This case sets up aced and checks only the Hugging Face row. The fix for the finding on install.sh line 983 changes what it expects.

groups.title: The plan: §3.5 and its decision
groups.kicker: The install plan records the uninstall design and why a separate script lost
intro: The install plan gains §3.5, "Uninstall", with what the target removes and keeps in each mode, and how field.one/uninstall.sh will run it. §4 records the decision that uninstall is a target of the one installer. A separate uninstall.sh in this repository, and a TypeScript-only field uninstall, lost because each would need its own copy of the data directory's resolution and of the ownership tests. §5 adds criteria, §6 marks chunks 3 and 4 shipped and adds this one as chunk 5, and §10.3 records the first real install from GitHub.
The plan stays in-progress, and this change opens no question. §7.4, on which domain serves the installer, is still open from before this change, although chunk 4 shipped field.one.

checks.text: §3.5's "The model weights stay" bullet makes the claim the finding on install.sh line 983 corrects: field-aced's weights are in ~/.field/models/acestep, not the Hugging Face cache.
§4's new decision says why uninstall is a target of the one installer, and why removing the Hugging Face cache lost.

groups.title: User docs
groups.kicker: Uninstall instructions, and field.one as the install URL
intro: docs/install.md replaces the manual rm -rf and pnpm remove -g field with field uninstall, and adds the target to both target tables. The README, docs/install.md, and docs/cli.md lead with curl -fsSL https://field.one/install.sh | bash. docs/release.md's example bumps patch, since releases are patch bumps from here on.

checks.text: field.one answers 404 for uninstall.sh today, and will until a release carries the target and audiofield deploys the file. curl -fsSL https://field.one/install.sh | bash -s -- uninstall works as soon as the release ships. The review lists this as a suggestion.
This paragraph makes the same Hugging Face claim as the finding on install.sh line 983.
